statement: For a deterministic nonempty finite path family taking one site per finite layer V_t of independent standard Gaussian weights, and deterministic real path offsets, M=max_p(c_p+sum_t g(t,p_t)) satisfies Var(M)=sum_t 1/|V_t|+Var(M(R)), where R removes each layer mean. In the source planar model Var(M_n)>=H_n; a fixed width W yields Var(M)>=n/W.
assumptions: Finite deterministic path family and finite deterministic offsets
Independent N(0,1) weights across all sites/layers

statement: For each N>=3, a fixed unit-Gaussian origin followed by N layers of N iid unit-Gaussian sites, with all edges between consecutive layers, has n=N+1-vertex free-endpoint maximum M_N. Var(M_N)=Theta(N/log N), so it satisfies the logarithmic variance premise but fails every fixed n^(1-epsilon) upper bound. At OU time s_N=N^(-1/2), the probability that the maximizing path changes tends to one, while its normalized common-vertex overlap tends to one in expectation and in probability.
assumptions: A triangular sequence of complete layered graphs: width and degree grow with N
Independent standard Gaussian site weights and independent standard Gaussian OU copies
All deterministic allowed paths visit the fixed origin and one site from each layer
OU parameter is time, not fresh-noise standard deviation
proof_or_counterexample: M_N=G_0+sum of N independent maxima T_N. Elementary Mills-tail moment bounds give Var(T_m)=Theta(1/log m). A uniform top-two gap density bound and a two-coordinates-in-a-short-interval event give c m^(-1/2)log m<=q_m(m^(-1/2))<=C m^(-1/4)log m+2m^(-3). Entire original/fresh arrays are independent across layers, so unchanged probability=(1-q_N)^N and expected overlap=n-Nq_N.
remaining_gap: Independent referee must verify the uniform gap-density estimate and mismatch lower event. The graph is not the fixed planar nearest-neighbor lattice; C0120 and any correctly quantified overlap bridge remain unresolved.
